clue.text: (and 4) The boys of Tonypandy used to speak

definitions.text: The boys of Tonypandy used to speak
definitions.note: defines the full name, first name here and surname at 4

parts.note: surface reading: a gang of lads from a Welsh mining town
setter's reading: the man made Viscount Tonypandy, who was formerly Speaker of the House of Commons, and whose name is two boys' first names

explanation.surface: Recalling how the lads of a Welsh valley town used to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonypandy is a town in the Rhondda; George Thomas, Speaker of the Commons 1976-83, became Viscount Tonypandy. His two names are both boys' names, hence 'The boys'. This light holds the first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh politician ennobled as Viscount Tonypandy had earlier presided over the House of Commons as its Speaker.

clue.text: Minimum intelligence from torch?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the faintest trace of understanding

definitions.note: a phrase for what a torch gives out
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a faint wavering light, such as a weak torch gives

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks how little brainpower a torch has; the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a faint gleam of light and a tiny trace of something such as hope or comprehension.

clue.text: Alternative to one about the alternative

indicators.note: the last word is read as one that goes about, that is round, the word before it

parts.note: the second alternative: the little word that offers a choice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A riddling line about choosing between one option and another.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's first and last words look like the same idea twice; the first is the definition, the last stands for the word of choice placed round the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Other, as in the other way, means a different or alternative choice from the one already given.

clue.text: Report of Sally on side of deck

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the surname is wanted for its sound

parts.note: Sally Gunnell, British Olympic hurdles champion of 1992

explanation.surface: A news account of a woman called Sally standing on a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors say GUNWALE as 'gunnel', the same sound as the athlete's surname. 'Report' looks like a gunshot alongside it, but signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The gunwale is the upper edge of a vessel's side, running along the edge of the deck.

clue.text: (See 1)

definitions.note: this light continues the name clued at 1 across

parts.note: surface reading: an instruction to look elsewhere
setter's reading: the clue at 1 across defines the whole name, and this light holds the surname

explanation.walkthrough: The clue at 1 across gives the former Speaker George Thomas, Viscount Tonypandy; this light takes his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas is the surname of the Welsh Labour politician who served as Speaker and took the Tonypandy title.

clue.text: Irish copper in cover was fatal to Samson

definitions.note: a clause; read as 'what was fatal to Samson'

indicators.note: the first pair of items are placed in, that is inside, the covering word

parts.note: a hat covers the head
standard abbreviation for Irish
chemical symbol for copper, from Latin cuprum

explanation.surface: An Irish policeman under cover brought about a biblical strongman's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal. The definition is a clause standing for the thing that killed Samson.
explanation.definitionFit: Delilah had Samson's locks shorn, and losing his hair robbed him of his strength, leading to his death.

clue.text: Add up to promotion, as on the 9 menu

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to add is to sum
hype is aggressive publicity
taken as written

explanation.surface: Totting up the cost of an advertising campaign, as listed on a menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is FISH AND CHIP SHOP; mushy peas, mashed marrowfat peas, are a standard British chip-shop side dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Mashed marrowfat peas are a classic side served alongside fried fish in British chippies.

clue.text: Get drunk around the West Indies? Not so fast!

indicators.note: the verb wraps around the islands, holding them inside

parts.note: to slosh drink is to swig it, and sloshed means drunk
standard abbreviation for the West Indies

explanation.surface: A warning to slow down to someone getting drunk around the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads as a rebuke to a drinker, but defines a pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only fairly slow moves at a speed that is not especially quick.

clue.text: Sign on the first part of 9

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Libra, the zodiac sign pictured as a balance

definitions.note: a phrase for what covers a fish
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the plates covering the skin of a fish, the first word of 9

explanation.walkthrough: 9 is FISH AND CHIP SHOP, whose first part is FISH. Libra's symbol is a pair of weighing balances.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra's emblem is a weighing balance, and a fish's body is covered with small overlapping bony plates.

clue.text: Female is to pass fruit in sack to takeaway

parts.note: standard abbreviation for female
taken as written
to hand something over is to pass it

indicators.note: the fruit is put in, that is inside, the word for dismissal

parts.note: getting the chop means getting the sack
rose hips, the fruit of the wild rose

explanation.surface: A woman is to hand over fruit in a bag to a takeaway shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like a bag but means dismissal, and the fruit splits it in two. Rose hips are the red fruit of wild roses.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling fried fish and chips to carry away is a classic British takeaway outlet.

clue.text: Sloy to film buffs in Asia Minor

definitions.note: a place description; read as 'place in Asia Minor'

parts.note: taken as written: an S followed by the surname Loy
film fans know Loy as the actress Myrna Loy, so her first name stands in for her surname

explanation.surface: Cinema enthusiasts in Turkey have their own way of saying an odd word.
explanation.walkthrough: Split Sloy as S plus Loy; Myrna Loy was the Hollywood star of The Thin Man, so movie fans swap her surname for her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Smyrna was the ancient Greek port on the Anatolian coast, now the Turkish city of Izmir.

clue.text: Girl holding king to bathe in bran tub

indicators.note: the girl's name holds, that is keeps inside it, the royal letter

parts.note: a girl's name
K is the chess and cards abbreviation for king
a dip is a quick bathe

explanation.surface: A girl carrying a king to wash him in a tub of bran.
explanation.walkthrough: A bran tub is a British fete game where children rummage in bran for hidden prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both names describe the same fairground game of fishing blindly for a wrapped prize buried in a container.

clue.text: Crazy food at Christmas party

definitions.meaning: first meaning: mad, in British slang
second meaning: savoury biscuits, and the paper tubes pulled with a bang at Christmas

explanation.walkthrough: The second half works two ways: crackers are biscuits eaten with cheese, and Christmas crackers are the festive party novelties pulled at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word for someone mad, and it also names thin biscuits and festive bang-snapping table novelties.

clue.text: Fellow member gets up and is…

parts.note: co- as in co-worker, a fellow
a Member of Parliament
rising is getting up

explanation.surface: An MP stands up to speak, and the sentence trails off.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots show the definition needs completing: 'is made up of'.
explanation.definitionFit: To comprise is to consist of, so the verb says what a whole is made up of.

clue.text: Article on the peg to acquire first set

parts.note: a golf tee is the peg the ball sits on
the definite article

explanation.surface: Putting an item on a hook to start a collection.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across entry 'on' puts the article after the peg. 'Set' looks like a collection but is a set of teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies teethe as their milk teeth come through, which is their first set of teeth.

clue.text: Sci-fi writer in love with Mavis?

indicators.note: being in love suggests a giddy, disordered state, so these letters are tumbled

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, shaped like the letter O
a woman's name taken as written

explanation.surface: A science-fiction author who has fallen for a woman named Mavis.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the anagram signal is loose. Isaac Asimov wrote I, Robot.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was a prolific American author of science fiction such as the Foundation series.

clue.text: (and 17) Naval rating Des makes provision for 9

definitions.note: defines the whole condiment pair, first half here and the rest at 17

indicators.note: the letters make, that is form, something new once rearranged

parts.note: a sailor called Des, taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor named Des lays on supplies for the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters give the whole two-light answer; this light holds its first two words and 17 down the last. 9 is FISH AND CHIP SHOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The classic seasonings shaken over fish and chips are provided at every British chip-shop counter.

clue.text: See 16

definitions.note: this light continues the answer clued at 16 down

parts.note: surface reading: an instruction to look elsewhere
setter's reading: the clue at 16 down supplies the wordplay for both lights, and this one holds the last word

explanation.walkthrough: The anagram at 16 down gives the chip-shop condiment pair; this light takes the final word.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt-based sour seasoning is the second half of the classic pair sprinkled over fish and chips.

clue.text: Forcibly lift surrounding setters with nostalgia

indicators.note: the lifting verb surrounds the setters, enclosing them

parts.note: to hoick is to yank upwards
a setter calls himself me, so several setters are mes

explanation.surface: Hauling up a group of crossword compilers who are longing for the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves as 'me' in clues, so the plural stands for several of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being homesick means pining for one's home, a kind of nostalgic longing.

clue.text: Hope it's displayed on the 9 menu!

indicators.note: displayed suggests set out in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wish to see a favourite dish listed at the chippy.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is FISH AND CHIP SHOP, which often sells pies kept warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm pies are a regular item sold alongside fried fish at British chip shops.

clue.text: Epilepsy a disqualification on the coast of India?

parts.note: French for illness, as in grand mal and petit mal epilepsy
taken as written
a bar is a ban that rules someone out

explanation.surface: Asking whether a medical condition disqualifies someone along India's shoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits Malabar is one stretch of coast, not the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The Malabar Coast is the long south-western shoreline of the Indian peninsula, in Kerala and Karnataka.

clue.text: Fight against nurse?

parts.note: as in pros and cons, con means against
to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: Someone resisting a hospital nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend is to struggle or compete against an opponent.

clue.text: A pipe of wine with fashionable entry

indicators.note: the wine comes with an entry, something let into it

parts.note: red Bordeaux wine
in means fashionable; entry marks where it goes

explanation.surface: A cask of wine let into a stylish party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' looks like a wine cask, a meaning it really has, but here it is a wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a single-reed woodwind instrument, and pipe is a general word for a wind instrument.

clue.text: Express sorrow at unconvincing part of the Bible

parts.note: a lame excuse is an unconvincing one
New Testament

explanation.surface: Grieving over a passage of scripture that fails to persuade.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament is to mourn or show grief aloud, a verb of mourning.

clue.text: Lighter in appropriate colour?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stick struck to make a flame

definitions.note: a phrase for a colour that goes with another
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a shade that goes with another, as in a good colour pairing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' looks like a paler comparative of a colour, but it is a thing that lights.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is a small stick for kindling flame, and colours that match go well together.

clue.text: South African custom: the person now at the wicket is on the 9 menu

parts.note: abbreviation for South Africa
established practice

parts.words: the person now at the wicket
parts.note: in cricket the batter currently batting is in

explanation.surface: A South African cricket tradition mentioned beside a chip-shop menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is FISH AND CHIP SHOP. At cricket the one at the wicket is the batter who is in.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-fried battered banger, a banger being a sausage, is a standard British chip-shop item.

clue.text: (and 26) Alien desired to keep light to race horse

definitions.note: defines the horse's full name, first word here and second at 26

indicators.note: the jumbled word keeps the light, holding it inside
something alien is strange and foreign, so these letters are made unfamiliar

parts.note: taken as written
a torch is a portable light

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial longs to hold a lamp while racing a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds the horse's whole name across this light and 26. Desert Orchid, a grey steeplechaser, won the 1989 Cheltenham Gold Cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert Orchid was a hugely popular British steeplechaser, a racehorse famed in the 1980s.

clue.text: (See 25)

definitions.note: this light continues the name clued at 25 across

parts.note: surface reading: an instruction to look elsewhere
setter's reading: the clue at 25 across builds the horse's whole name, and this light holds the second word

explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay at 25 across gives the famous grey steeplechaser; this light takes the second word of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The flower name forms the second half of the celebrated grey jumper's racing name.
